findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff adds a bare gitlink 'sentry-repo' at the repository root with no corresponding .gitmodules entry, so it cannot be cloned or checked out and the Snuba-side sample_weight support it implies is never actually wired into the test environment. Any fresh clone or CI checkout fails at 'sentry-repo' (git submodule update --init errors with 'no submodule mapping found in .gitmodules'), and the SnubaTestCase assertions on sample_weight-derived counts (data[0][1][0]['count'] == 10) have no code path in this diff that produces a sample_weight column, so the endpoint tests fail against real infrastructure.

[BUG] _should_apply_sample_weight_transform imports sentry.snuba.discover/errors/transactions inside the function and compares with ==, but the dataset object passed from organization_events_stats is the endpoint's dataset class instance, and the upsampled_count function is only registered in discover.py's function_converter, so when the errors dataset does not share that converter the transformed column 'upsampled_count() as count' is an unknown function and the query errors. Requests hitting the stats endpoint on the errors dataset (where _should_apply_sample_weight_transform unconditionally returns True) execute a SnQL query containing upsampled_count(), which the resolver rejects unless it happens to inherit discover's function_converter — the success of the entire path rests on an undocumented inheritance relationship; if it doesn't hold, every allowlisted errors query 500s.

[BUG] Constructing SnubaParams(start=None, end=None, projects=self.projects) violates SnubaParams' post-init validation, which dereferences start/end, raising TypeError/UnreachableQuery instead of producing a usable params object. ErrorUpsamplingTest.setUp crashes for every test in the class, so the helper module ships with zero passing unit coverage.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint test mocks sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options, but the cache (sentry.utils.cache) persists across requests for 60 seconds keyed only on org id + project-id hash, so a second request with a changed allowlist (or a test hitting the same org) reads the stale cached eligibility and bypasses the option check entirely. An operator who removes a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist keeps getting upsampled (inflated) counts for up to 60 seconds, and any test or code path that reuses org/project ids will see the previous decision; the only invalidation hook (invalidate_upsampling_cache) has no caller in this diff.

[ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling writes a top-level 'sample_rate' field onto normalized data, but nothing in this diff (beyond the unwired sentry-repo gitlink) establishes that 'sample_rate' survives event normalization or maps to the 'sample_weight' column the upsampled_count SnQL aggregate reads, so the end-to-end path from test fixture to Column('sample_weight') is unproven. If normalization drops the unknown sample_rate field (the standard behavior for unrecognized top-level keys), sum(sample_weight) aggregates over a non-existent/zero column and the endpoint tests asserting count==10 fail or silently return wrong data; the factory helper becomes dead weight producing a false sense of coverage.

[BUG] The `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is registered only in the discover dataset, but `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` gates the transformation on `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returning True unconditionally for the errors dataset, so queries routed to the errors dataset receive the column `upsampled_count() as count` that no function registry knows and fail to resolve. Any request hitting organization_events_stats with the errors dataset over an all-allowlisted org gets a 500/invalid-function Snuba error instead of stats; the tests never exercise the errors dataset (all test URLs use the default discover dataset), so this path is entirely unverified.

[BUG] Only the literal string `count()` is transformed, while every sibling aggregation over the same sampled data (`count_unique(...)`, `count_if(...)`, `percent(...)`, `failure_count()`, any `count() as alias`) passes through untouched, producing mixed upsampled/un-upsampled numbers in a single response. Users querying a fully-allowlisted org with yAxis like `count(),count_unique(user)` see count inflated by 1/sample_rate while unique-user counts stay at sampled values — internally inconsistent charts that no test in the diff covers.

[ADVISORY] The 60-second eligibility cache is never invalidated anywhere: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has zero callers in this diff, so allowlist removals take up to 60 seconds to propagate and the helper is an inert API. Operators removing a project from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` keep serving sum(sample_weight)-based counts for that project for up to a minute; also any drift between cache and option state shows as unexplained count jumps, and the unused invalidation function is dead code.

[ADVISORY] The only code in the diff that derives sampling data from `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` is in the test factory (`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` setting `sample_rate`), while the query side reads the `sample_weight` column — no production ingestion/normalization path in this diff writes `sample_weight` from the client context. The endpoint tests pass because the factory fabricates the value, but real events from clients reporting `error_sampling.client_sample_rate` have no writer for `sample_weight`, so `sum(sample_weight)` yields null/0 counts in production until the ingestion-side change lands — the tests verify a pipeline that only exists in test fixtures.

[ADVISORY] Discover-dataset queries without a literal `event.type:error` string in the raw query (e.g. the default issue-list query, or `event.type:error` expressed via the saved query/preset rather than the query param) skip upsampling entirely, so error counts for allowlisted orgs silently differ depending on how the filter is spelled. Dashboard widgets and saved queries that filter errors via any path other than the exact `event.type:error` substring in `request.GET['query']` show un-upsampled (10x lower) counts for the same data, an inconsistency users cannot diagnose; no test covers discover queries with implicit error filtering.

[ADVISORY] The new endpoint tests never clear or bypass the 60-second `error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{projects}` cache, and the endpoint caches eligibility on first request per test class, so test methods sharing org/project ids can consume a stale eligibility decision from a previously run test with a different mocked allowlist. Developers running the suite get order-dependent flaky assertions (e.g. `test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist` reading a True cached from the prior full-allowlist test), since `mock.patch` of options only affects the cache-miss path.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a new git submodule 'sentry-repo' pointing at an external commit that is unrelated to the error-upsampling feature. Every engineer and CI job that pulls this branch now clones an unexplained external repository pinned to a5d2909; nothing in the PR description or the upsampling requirement justifies it, and reviewers/maintainers get bitten at merge time when an unvetted dependency enters the tree.

[BUG] invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but no code anywhere in the diff (option update handler, admin action, signal receiver, or test) ever calls it, so the 60-second eligibility cache can never be proactively invalidated. Operators who flip issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist see stale upsampling decisions for up to 60 seconds on the exact project-set keys that were previously cached; the function is a ships-inert public surface with zero writers.

[ADVISORY] The diff silently rewrites the pre-existing validation error message from "If topEvents needs to be at least 1" to "topEvents needs to be at least 1", which is cosmetic work not traceable to the upsampling requirement. Any client or test asserting the old message string breaks; the change rides along in a feature PR where reviewers scanning for risk will miss it.

[ADVISORY] The diff modifies the global store_event factory so that every event, in every test in the entire suite, gets a sample_rate synthesized from contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate — a change to shared test infrastructure far broader than the stated error-upsampling endpoint scope. Any existing test that stores an event with an error_sampling context and asserts on the stored event's sample_rate (or on data derived from it) now sees altered fixture data; the coupling is invisible to future contributors adding error_sampling contexts for unrelated reasons, and the upsampling feature itself never reads normalized sample_rate (it relies on the snuba sample_weight column), so the traceability of this hook to the requirement is unclear.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint now writes the eligibility decision into a 60-second shared cache keyed only by org id and project-id tuple, layering a caching/consistency mechanism into the API endpoint that the stated requirement (upsampled error counts) does not call for. During a rolling allowlist change, two identical requests within 60 seconds can receive different count semantics (raw count vs sum(sample_weight)), producing visible count jumps of ~10x for users watching dashboards; the broad cache key also means a request with a different dataset/query shape reuses the same cached allowlist decision even though _should_apply_sample_weight_transform is re-evaluated per request, a split the code comments assert but nothing enforces.

[BUG] Error-query detection is a lowercase substring match on `event.type:error`, so discover-dataset queries that return only errors without that literal token (no event.type filter, `event.type:!transaction`) are silently not upsampled. For allowlisted projects, an Issues/Discover dashboard querying errors without an explicit `event.type:error` token returns raw (downsampled) counts while the identical query with the filter returns upsampled counts — users see counts differ by the sample factor between two semantically equivalent queries, and the unfiltered query understates error volume.

[BUG] The substring check `"event.type:error" in query` matches negated and embedded tokens, so `!event.type:error` (a transactions query) and quoted values containing the token classify as error queries. A discover query `!event.type:error` over allowlisted projects gets `count()` rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)`, applying error upsampling weights to transaction events that have no sample_weight, producing wrong (or erroring) counts for that dashboard.

[BUG] `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True when `dataset == errors`, but the `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is registered only in discover.py's function_converter, so errors-dataset queries execute with a y-axis function the errors dataset cannot resolve. The stats endpoint hit with the errors dataset (or any scoped dataset that doesn't inherit discover's function table) on allowlisted projects fails to resolve `upsampled_count()` in the query builder, returning a 500 instead of the timeseries.

[ADVISORY] Only the y-axis column list is transformed; `count()` appearing in equations (`equations=self.get_equation_list(...)`) and in the top-events ordering/selection path is left as raw `count()`. A user on an allowlisted project issuing an equation like `count()/user()` or topEvents ranked by raw count gets a series mixing upsampled counts with unupsampled counts inside one response — the ratio is off by the sample factor and the top-N ranking disagrees with the displayed series.

[ADVISORY] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has no caller anywhere in this diff, and the cache key is a per-(org, project-set) composite, so an operator flipping the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option cannot invalidate entries for the arbitrary project-set keys already cached. After an operator adds a project to the allowlist, stats endpoints serve stale non-upsampled counts for up to 60s per project-combination key, and the provided invalidation helper is dead code that cannot enumerate those keys — the invalidation story the docstring promises does not exist.

[ADVISORY] The 60s cache is keyed only on (org_id, project_ids) and stores the allowlist result, but the allowlist option is org-independent (a single global `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`), producing unbounded distinct cache keys as every project-combination gets its own entry. Organizations querying many distinct project subsets (dashboards, alerts with rotating project filters) fill the shared cache with combinatorially many keys, each pinning a stale copy of the same global option for 60s; the cache stores a value that is a pure function of project_ids and one global option, so a single project-level key would do.

[ADVISORY] The design mixes units across projects: queries where all projects are allowlisted return upsampled counts, while any query that includes one non-allowlisted project returns raw counts, with no indication to the caller which semantics the response uses. Saved dashboards/alerts that span allowlisted and non-allowlisted projects silently drop from upsampled to raw counts depending on which projects the user selects, so threshold-based alert rules fire at different real volumes for the same issue depending on project selection, with no field in the response distinguishing the two modes.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a git submodule `sentry-repo` pointing at an external commit, meaning the actual ingestion-side piece that populates `sample_weight` lives outside this repository, and the only in-repo writer is a test factory (`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling`). Main-repo deployments without the exact submodule commit registered query `sum(sample_weight)` against an events table where nothing populates the column, so allowlisted projects get counts of 0/null instead of upsampled counts; the helper module's assumption "schema ensures sample_weight exists" is unverifiable and unenforced in this codebase.

[ADVISORY] `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` is applied unconditionally inside `store_event`, mutating every event stored by every test in the suite when an `error_sampling` context is present, and silently swallows all exceptions with bare `except Exception: pass`. Test authors storing events with an `error_sampling` context now get a `sample_rate` injected without opting in, so existing tests asserting on `sample_rate` semantics drift; the blanket except also hides malformed-context bugs that the ingest path would surface in production.

[BUG] The cache key uses Python's built-in hash(), which is randomized per process, so the same (org, project_ids) pair produces different keys across workers and the 60s cache almost never hits. The 'performance optimization' that this PR's title claims never materializes in production: every request on a cache-miss prefix re-runs the option lookup, and the cache additionally fills with divergent duplicate keys; the stated objective of the change is silently not delivered.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff, so allowlist configuration changes are never propagated to the 60s cache. When an operator removes a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist, that project's queries keep being upsampled (returning inflated counts) for up to 60 seconds — or indefinitely longer if hash-randomization splits keys and stale entries are never invalidated; the docstring's claimed consistency mechanism does not exist.

[ADVISORY] _is_error_focused_query silently reduces the feature's scope to only queries containing the literal string 'event.type:error', dropping any discover-dataset error query that omits the filter or spells it differently (e.g. quoted or uppercase 'event.type:Error'). Users on allowlisted projects running discover queries without an explicit event.type:error filter get non-upsampled (under)counts while identical queries with the filter get upsampled counts — a split-brain count that changes results depending on how the query is phrased; the comment 'Reduced to only check ... to err on the side of caution' is the only record that this narrowing was accepted, with no human sign-off visible in the artifact.

[ADVISORY] In the top_events path only y_axes/timeseries_columns are transformed; raw_groupby (get_field_list) and orderby (get_orderby) still reference the original count(), so top events are ranked by unupsampled count while the displayed series uses upsampled_count. A user on an allowlisted project requesting topEvents ordered by count() gets rows ordered by raw event counts but y-axis values multiplied by sample weight — the top-N ranking can disagree with the plotted values (e.g. a rarely-sampled event showing the largest number but not ranked first).

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a 'sentry-repo' gitlink (subproject commit a5d290951de...) that has nothing to do with the upsampling feature. Every consumer of this repository gets an unrequested submodule pinned to an opaque commit; CI and downstream packaging can break or silently pull unknown code, and the intent of the PR (error upsampling) is obscured by an unrelated artifact.

[ADVISORY] The diff changes the unrelated topEvents validation message from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1' inside a feature PR about error upsampling. Any client or test asserting the old error string breaks; the change is scope drift unrelated to the accepted upsampling objective and appears to be review-iteration drift smuggled into the PR.

[ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling is wired unconditionally into store_event, mutating normalized_data['sample_rate'] for every event created by every test in the suite, not just upsampling tests. Test authors storing events with an error_sampling context now get a different stored payload (an injected sample_rate) than before, which can change results of unrelated event-processing and search tests — the factory's behavior changed globally to serve this one feature without any gating.

[BUG] The endpoint tests mock options but exercise the real 60s cache in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, so eligibility computed in one test (keyed by org+project_ids) leaks into the next test that reuses the same organization. test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist and test_error_upsampling_with_no_allowlisted_projects can read a cached True from test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects and assert against upsampled counts that were never configured, producing order-dependent flaky failures — and worse, masking real regressions where the allowlist path is not actually consulted.

[ADVISORY] The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is registered without `private=True`, unlike the adjacent internal functions, making it part of the public function-converter surface for any organization. Any authenticated user of any org can pass `yAxis=upsampled_count()` (or reference it in saved queries/dashboards) and get `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` over events where `sample_weight` is NULL or unset for non-allowlisted projects, returning 0/garbage counts — and exposing the existence of the internal sampling column to tenants never enrolled in the program.

[ADVISORY] The 60-second eligibility cache stores only the allowlist verdict keyed by org+project_ids, so a project removed from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` continues to receive upsampled (10x-inflated) counts for up to 60 seconds, and the provided `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere in the diff. Operators who remove a project from the allowlist during an incident (e.g., because sample_weight data is corrupt) cannot stop the inflated counts without waiting out the cache or deploying code, since the invalidation hook is dead.

[ADVISORY] `_is_error_focused_query` uses a raw substring check `"event.type:error" in query` on the lowercased query string, so any query containing that literal — including negated (`!event.type:error`) or otherwise-scoped queries — is classified as error-focused and gets `count()` silently rewritten to the sample-weight sum. A user issuing a Discover query like `!event.type:error` (transaction-focused via negation) on allowlisted projects gets upsampled counts over a result set the substring heuristic never validated, returning inflated numbers in dashboards with no error to signal the mismatch.

[ADVISORY] The cached eligibility verdict is stored per (org, project_ids) and reused across all requests and users, but the function also re-evaluates `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` on every call, so the two halves of the security/eligibility decision are computed against different points in time while the code comments claim the caching 'ensures consistent behavior across query execution'. Within the 60-second window, the dataset/request half of the decision reflects fresh state while the allowlist half is stale; a reviewer or operator auditing why upsampling fired cannot rely on either comment, and the mismatch between cached and fresh halves produces decisions that correspond to no actual configuration state.

[BUG] The partial-allowlist and no-allowlist endpoint tests do not clear the 'error_upsampling_eligible:*' cache between test methods, so they assert non-upsampled counts against a code path that can return a stale cached True from a prior test method. Django TestCase transaction rollback reuses the same project IDs across test methods in this class, and the in-process cache is not flushed, so test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects caches eligibility=True for the exact key that test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist then hits; the partial test receives upsampled counts (10) and fails on `assert data[0][1][0]['count'] == 1`, and when tests pass it is only because the cache happens to be cold — the tests verify cache state, not the allowlist logic they claim to check.

[ADVISORY] The module's public entry point is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects — including its 60-second cache write, cache-hit read, and the `cached_result and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(...)` short-circuit — has zero tests; only the private helpers are tested. A regression in the caching logic (e.g. caching before the dataset check so a transactions query permanently caches True, or the `cached_result and ...` returning a truthy non-bool) ships undetected while the suite stays green; operators relying on the 60s eventual-consistency guarantee have no coverage proving it exists.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no test anywhere in the diff (neither tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py nor test_organization_events_stats.py reference it) and no production caller is added in this diff. The invalidation function is dead-on-arrival code whose cache-key format (`hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`) is duplicated from the write site; a future edit to one key format and not the other silently breaks invalidation, and no test would catch the drift.

[ADVISORY] The upsampling column transform is applied in four distinct call sites (top_events RPC, top_events non-RPC, timeseries RPC, timeseries non-RPC) but every endpoint test in this diff queries without topEvents, so three of the four transformed call sites are never exercised with upsampling enabled. A regression where `final_columns` is computed but not passed on the top_events path (e.g. reverting one of the `y_axes=final_columns` lines back to `query_columns`) passes the entire new test class, and dashboards using topEvents against allowlisted projects silently report non-upsampled counts.

[ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling swallows every exception from a plain dict .get chain with `except Exception: pass`, and no test exercises a malformed contexts value (None, string, nested non-dict) through store_event. Because the guards are dead code for well-formed dicts, a future refactor of contexts to a non-dict type turns the whole helper into a silent no-op: events lose sample_rate, upsampling counts drop to raw counts, and no test fails since neither the helper nor the factory path has a test asserting sample_rate is set for any edge-case shape.

[BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling replaces count() with sum(sample_weight) for all events in allowlisted projects, but this diff contains no backfill or migration that populates sample_weight on existing error events. For any event written before the sample_weight pipeline exists (i.e., all historical data at deploy time), Column("sample_weight") is NULL, so sum(sample_weight) yields NULL per group and toInt64(NULL) produces 0/garbage — every pre-existing error event in an allowlisted project silently counts as 0 in org stats dashboards the moment the project is added to the allowlist. This is a read-new-column-before-backfill violation with silent data loss, not an error.

[BUG] The upsampled_count SnQL function reads a sample_weight column that no writer anywhere in this diff (or the event ingestion path it touches) produces — the only new writer is the test-only factory hook _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling, which sets sample_rate, not sample_weight. The feature ships inert-to-corrupting: even new events ingested after deploy carry no sample_weight (the normalization change in factories.py only affects test event storage and writes a differently-named field), so sum(sample_weight) is NULL/0 for 100% of rows and the upsampled count understates real error volume by the full amount rather than upsampling it. No dual-write exists between the old count() representation and the new sample_weight representation, so any later backfill/cutover will find nothing to migrate from.

[ADVISORY] Allowlist eligibility is cached for 60 seconds keyed only on (org, sorted project_ids), and invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called from any option-change hook in this diff. An operator removing a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist sees upsampled (data-losing, sample_weight-backed) queries continue for up to 60 seconds after the config change, and the invalidate helper exists but nothing invokes it — the config rollback path for this data-affecting transform is effectively 60s of stale skew with no documented invalidation.

[BUG] The 60-second eligibility cache returns stale allowlist decisions with no invalidation wired up, so requests made within 60s of an allowlist change apply (or skip) the upsampled_count() transformation inconsistently with the actual option value. invalidate_upsampling_cache() is defined but has zero call sites in this diff, so when a project is removed from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist, up to 60 seconds of requests still query sum(sample_weight) on events that are no longer being written with that field, producing silently wrong counts reported as HTTP 200 success.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query only matches the literal substring 'event.type:error' in the raw query string, so any discover query that filters errors by other means (issue id, 'level:error', 'event.type:errored' OR-combined, or a query where 'event.type:error' is negated with '!' or excluded with '-') is treated as a non-error query and silently skips upsampling. Users on fully-allowlisted projects running discover queries like 'level:error' or 'is:unresolved' get raw count() (unweighted, ~10x undercount for 0.1 sample rate) returned as a successful 200 with no error, warning, or log — the numbers are wrong by the sampling factor and nothing surfaces it.

[BUG] The upsampled_count SnQLFunction is registered only in the discover dataset's function_converter, but is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects returns True for the errors dataset too, so error-dataset requests will emit a query containing a function the errors dataset cannot resolve. Any request that reaches _get_event_stats with the errors dataset and allowlisted projects gets a Snuba 'unknown function upsampled_count' style failure surfacing as a raw 500 instead of either a 4xx or untransformed results.

[BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling relies on the assumption that every event in allowlisted projects has sample_weight populated, but events ingested before upsampling was enabled (or via any writer that doesn't set the context) have no sample_weight, so sum(sample_weight) silently drops them. Historical/pre-rollout events in an allowlisted project contribute 0 to upsampled_count() (null in the sum), so charts silently lose all pre-existing error volume with a 200 success and no indication any events were skipped — the code comment explicitly asserts 'no additional null checks are needed' with nothing in this diff enforcing it.

[ADVISORY] The transform only rewrites the exact literal 'count()'; count() appearing inside equations (yAxis 'equation|count()/2'), count_unique(...), or other count-family aggregates in query_columns passes through unchanged while the plain count() is upsampled. Dashboard widget and stats requests that mix 'count()' with equations or count_unique get internally inconsistent series — the upsampled count() column and the untransformed count inside the equation are computed on different weightings in the same 200 response, and the mismatch is invisible to the user.

[ADVISORY] The cache key hashes only organization.id and the sorted project_ids, not the allowlist option version or dataset/query shape, and cache.set stores the decision even when eligibility is False for a transient reason (e.g., options plugin returning a default before a remote option store is warm). A transient options backend hiccup that returns [] for issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist gets cached as 'not eligible' for 60 seconds org-wide, silently serving unweighted (undercounted) error stats as success during that window; operators debugging this see no error anywhere because the miss is indistinguishable from a legitimate False.

[ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling wraps its context lookup and float conversion in bare 'except Exception: pass' blocks, swallowing all errors including programming errors like a contexts value being a non-mapping. Test fixtures silently store events with no sample_rate whenever the error_sampling context is malformed (e.g., contexts.error_sampling is a string, causing AttributeError on .get), so test runs pass while exercising events that don't match the production ingestion path the upsampling query depends on — a fixture/production drift that hides real breakage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff adds a bare gitlink 'sentry-repo' at the repository root with no corresponding .gitmodules entry, so it cannot be cloned or checked out and the Snuba-side sample_weight support it implies is never actually wired into the test environment. Any fresh clone or CI checkout fails at 'sentry-repo' (git submodule update --init errors with 'no submodule mapping found in .gitmodules'), and the SnubaTestCase assertions on sample_weight-derived counts (data[0][1][0]['count'] == 10) have no code path in this diff that produces a sample_weight column, so the endpoint tests fail against real infrastructure.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a gitlink entry at repo root (`sentry-repo`, mode 160000) without adding/updating a `.gitmodules` file, so `git submodule update --init` would indeed have no mapping for it. However, the finding’s broader claims (that fresh clones/CI necessarily fail and that the sample_weight path is “never wired” so the new upsampling tests must fail) are not verifiable from the diff: a normal clone can still succeed without initializing submodules, and the diff does introduce an `upsampled_count()` SnQL function plus sets `sample_rate` during event storage, which could be sufficient depending on existing (out-of-diff) ingestion/schema behavior. Any request that reaches _get_event_stats with the errors dataset and allowlisted projects gets a Snuba 'unknown function upsampled_count' style failure surfacing as a raw 500 instead of either a 4xx or untransformed results.

adjudication.rationale: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling()` rewrites `count()` into `upsampled_count() as count`. `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform()` explicitly returns `True` when `dataset == errors`, so `organization_events_stats._get_event_stats` will pass `upsampled_count()` to Snuba for the errors dataset when projects are allowlisted. In this diff, `upsampled_count` is only registered as a `SnQLFunction` in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`'s `function_converter`; there is no corresponding registration shown for the errors dataset. That makes it likely that errors-dataset queries will reference an unknown function and fail at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling relies on the assumption that every event in allowlisted projects has sample_weight populated, but events ingested before upsampling was enabled (or via any writer that doesn't set the context) have no sample_weight, so sum(sample_weight) silently drops them. Historical/pre-rollout events in an allowlisted project contribute 0 to upsampled_count() (null in the sum), so charts silently lose all pre-existing error volume with a 200 success and no indication any events were skipped — the code comment explicitly asserts 'no additional null checks are needed' with nothing in this diff enforcing it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does replace `count()` with `upsampled_count()` for allowlisted error queries (`transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`), and `upsampled_count` is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no `coalesce/ifNull` handling (see `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`). The helper’s doc/comment explicitly assumes `sample_weight` exists and is populated for all relevant events, but nothing in this diff enforces that invariant for existing/historical events (the only ingestion-related change sets `sample_rate`, not `sample_weight`). So there is a concrete, diff-grounded risk that events without `sample_weight` won’t contribute to the sum, but whether such events actually exist (e.g., pre-rollout) is not provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The transform only rewrites the exact literal 'count()'; count() appearing inside equations (yAxis 'equation|count()/2'), count_unique(...), or other count-family aggregates in query_columns passes through unchanged while the plain count() is upsampled. Dashboard widget and stats requests that mix 'count()' with equations or count_unique get internally inconsistent series — the upsampled count() column and the untransformed count inside the equation are computed on different weightings in the same 200 response, and the mismatch is invisible to the user.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, upsampling is implemented by `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling()` which only rewrites columns whose normalized string equals exactly `"count()"` (see `if column_lower == "count()": ...`). In `organization_events_stats._get_event_stats`, only the `query_columns` passed as `y_axes` / `timeseries_columns` / `selected_columns` are transformed to `final_columns`, while equations are still passed via `equations=self.get_equation_list(...)` without any corresponding transformation. Therefore, if a request uses equations that embed `count()` (or other count-like functions) rather than the plain `count()` yAxis, the upsampling rewrite will not be applied consistently across all computed series within the same response. The exact end-user impact depends on how equations are parsed/resolved, which is not shown in the diff, so this is a concrete, diff-grounded edge-case/incompleteness rather than a fully provable broken behavior from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cache key hashes only organization.id and the sorted project_ids, not the allowlist option version or dataset/query shape, and cache.set stores the decision even when eligibility is False for a transient reason (e.g., options plugin returning a default before a remote option store is warm). A transient options backend hiccup that returns [] for issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist gets cached as 'not eligible' for 60 seconds org-wide, silently serving unweighted (undercounted) error stats as success during that window; operators debugging this see no error anywhere because the miss is indistinguishable from a legitimate False.

adjudication.rationale: In `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (new `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`), the allowlist eligibility (`is_eligible`) is cached for 60s purely on `organization.id` and the `project_ids` set (`cache_key = f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`). The code does cache negative results too (`cache.set(cache_key, is_eligible, 60)` even when `is_eligible` is `False`), and there is no integration shown that calls `invalidate_upsampling_cache`, so allowlist changes or transient misreads of `options.get(...)` could be masked for up to 60s for the same org+project set. However, the finding’s claim that dataset/query shape isn’t accounted for is overstated because `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)` is re-evaluated on every call (even on cache hits).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling wraps its context lookup and float conversion in bare 'except Exception: pass' blocks, swallowing all errors including programming errors like a contexts value being a non-mapping. Test fixtures silently store events with no sample_rate whenever the error_sampling context is malformed (e.g., contexts.error_sampling is a string, causing AttributeError on .get), so test runs pass while exercising events that don't match the production ingestion path the upsampling query depends on — a fixture/production drift that hides real breakage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` in `src/sentry/testutils/factories.py` and calls it from `Factories.store_event`. That helper wraps both the nested `.get(...)` chain and the `float(...)` conversion in broad `except Exception: pass` blocks, which will indeed swallow unexpected/programming errors (e.g., `contexts.error_sampling` being a non-mapping) and silently skip setting `normalized_data["sample_rate"]`. This is a diff-grounded test-fixture robustness/drift concern (it can hide malformed fixture data and make tests less faithful), but it’s not a concrete, demonstrated production correctness defect in this PR by itself.
